# SKILL — COMPARABLE RESEARCH

## Purpose
Create a defensible comparable set for valuation.

## Source priority
Tier A: specialist auction-house realised results; major/regional auction realised results; museum/maker archive/catalogue documentation.

Tier B: The Saleroom realised results; LiveAuctioneers; Invaluable; Barnebys; eBay SOLD/COMPLETED.

Tier C: specialist dealers; 1stDibs; reputable galleries/design dealers.

Tier D: Etsy; Vinted; general marketplace active listings. Tier D is context, not valuation evidence.

## Search method
1. exact maker + pattern/design + object type
2. maker + object type + colour/size
3. maker + closely related form
4. region/period + highly similar form only if maker remains uncertain

Do not start by collecting vague visual lookalikes.

## Comparable record
Capture object, attributed maker, date/period, dimensions, colour, condition, signed/labelled status, venue, sale date, estimate, realised/hammer price, premium status, currency, URL/reference and similarity notes.

## Similarity score
- 30 maker/pattern
- 15 object type
- 10 size
- 10 colour
- 10 age
- 10 condition
- 5 signed/labelled
- 5 venue credibility
- 5 recency

Then apply judgement.

## Reject as a primary comp when
Maker is materially different; object type unrelated; size differs greatly; condition exceptional/poor; result is a single outlier; only asking price exists; attribution is seller speculation; listing title is misleading.

## Output rule
Always label each price SOLD / REALISED, ESTIMATE, DEALER ASKING or MARKETPLACE ASKING. Do not average all four together.
